newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures finish lower as dlr drops.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures finish lower as dlr drops.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished lower across the board in dull trade on Monday as the dollar's decline offset the metal's further advance in London.

"Aluminium futures are slightly lower than their theoretical levels (calculated on the basis of LME prices and the foreign exchange rate)," said a trader at a major trading house. "But precious metals are more interesting."
Traders said bullish sentiment toward aluminium in London had failed to attract buying in Tokyo, as speculators saw better investment opportunities in the more volatile Tokyo precious metals market.
The dollar's decline below 115 yen weighed heavily on yen-based futures, although many participants believed the metal was heading towards $1,700 a tonne on the LME, traders said.

Benchmark April 1998 closed at 196.4 yen per kg, shedding 0.7 yen from the close on Friday. Other contracts ranged from 0.5 yen to 1.3 yen lower. Estimated volume was 2,216 lots, down from 3,737 lots on Friday.
